correctness.rationale: Every maximal clique is a surviving edge or an isolated singleton. Every mixed maximal stable set is exactly one deleted matching pair; side stable sets meet every edge, and isolated singleton cliques meet every maximal stable set. For each deleted pair, exactly (a-1)(b-1)-(t-1) surviving edges avoid both endpoints. These exhaustive classifications prove the formula and its zero/one cases. An independent brute-force subset enumerator verified all a,b<=5 and all legal t, plus crown cases through n=6. The finite computation is not used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted statement-level searches and inspection of the foundational CIS and almost-CIS literature found no exact enumeration of non-CIS pairs for a complete bipartite graph with a matching deleted. Known broader CIS structure recovers some zero/nonzero cases, and the 2009 almost-CIS theorem covers the defect-one consequence, but neither implies the exact defect count. The recent 2026 recognition paper full text was inaccessible, leaving a disclosed residual overlap risk rather than a fabricated whole-document exclusion.
residual_risks: The full text of arXiv:2608.11289 could not be retrieved through the accessible primary/OA routes during this review, so an uninspected passage could in principle overlap the family result.

value.rationale: The 2026 coNP-completeness result makes tractable exact CIS-certificate structure mathematically motivated. Deleting a matching is a canonical controlled perturbation of the basic CIS family K_{a,b}; the theorem gives a closed certificate count, a complete CIS stability boundary, and a cubic crown-graph specialization. This is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice, and the exact count contains information not supplied by mere recognition.
